Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Network Officer; David Ruiz, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.
Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q3 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas.
First, our subscriber growth exceeded expectations with robust net additions in residential and business segments. Second, we continue to see strong adoption of our new products like Ultra 5G Home FWA and StreamMax bundles, leading to significant revenue uplift and accelerated subscriber gains. Third, our service revenue growth in wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments delivered impressive year-over-year increases. Fourth, we are making significant strides in optimizing subscriber acquisition costs while maintaining low churn. Fifth, our EBITDA margins expanded meaningfully due to efficiency programs and revenue mix shifts, and finally, we are strategically enhancing spectrum utilization and planning future allocations to fuel 5G expansion.

Mike Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $7.1 billion, an increase of 8% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.71 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.2%, up 220 basis points year-over-year and 110 basis points sequentially. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in five years, reflecting the successful execution of our Efficiency 2.0 program alongside robust revenue growth from our converged telecom and media operations. Our trailing 12-month EBITDA margin now stands at 37.5%, positioning us ahead of peers like AT&T at 39% and Verizon at 36%, while trending toward the upper end of European incumbents like Vodafone's 38-40% range.
Let me break down the key drivers, trends, and regional nuances, with a forward-looking perspective. Margin expansion begins with top-line leverage. Wireless service revenues grew 8% year-over-year to $4.2 billion, driven by a 4.2% ARPU increase to $58.50—our highest ever—fueled by 5G standalone deployments and premium unlimited plans bundled with our StreamMax SVOD service. Postpaid net adds reached 450,000, with 5G penetration now at 62% of our 28 million subscriber base, up from 45% a year ago. This approach mirrors T-Mobile's ARPU strategy but with our media integration providing a sticky advantage: 35% of new 5G subscribers opted for StreamMax bundles, boosting blended ARPU by 2.5%. On fixed broadband, fiber-to-the-home passings expanded 15% to 12 million homes, driving 12% revenue growth and a 300 basis point mix shift toward higher-margin fiber at around 55% EBITDA versus legacy copper and DOCSIS at 42%. Media revenues at $1.8 billion grew 6% on advertising recovery and affiliate fee increases with MVPDs like Comcast, though partially offset by rising sports rights costs.
Operationally, we've captured 520 basis points in structural cost savings year-to-date through Efficiency 2.0, targeting $1.2 billion annually by fiscal 2024. Network optimization via AI-driven traffic management on Open RAN trials—now 20% of new sites partnering with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony—reduced energy costs by 18%, or $120 million annualized, even as data traffic rose 25% from 5G video streaming, improving power usage effectiveness to 1.35 from 1.45. In customer operations, RPA and GenAI chatbots handled 65% of Tier 1 support, cutting call center costs 22% or $85 million, with churn at a best-in-class 0.85% versus the industry's 1.1%. Procurement successes included renegotiated handset subsidies with Apple and Samsung saving $200 million and shifting 40% of backhaul to lit-wave deals with Zayo, compressing opex by 10%. SG&A fell to 14.2% of revenue from 16.1%, supported by zero-based budgeting.
Content and programming costs presented a headwind, with media at about 25% EBITDA contribution and expenses up 11% to $950 million from NBA and NFL renewals escalating 8-10% annually, similar to Disney's challenges. We're countering with owned IP: StreamMax originals like the Edge City franchise now account for 45% of viewing hours, reducing third-party licensing from 60% to 52%. Our FAST channels partnership with Roku generated $150 million in incremental ad revenue at 70% margins.
Regionally, North America at 75% of EBITDA achieved a 39.5% margin, up 300 basis points year-over-year, propelled by 5G Ultra Wideband in 85% of markets and spectrum efficiency from our 2022 C-band wins in 3.45-3.55 GHz, plus high-margin enterprise private 5G like Ford pilots at $200 per month per slice. Europe at 15% and 34.8% margin improved 100 basis points but trailed due to EU roaming caps and UK Ofcom regulations compressing ARPU 2%, offset by FTTH from our 2021 Spanish altnet acquisition. APAC and LatAm at 10% and 36.2% margin surged 400 basis points on organic 5G in Brazil and India using low-band 700 MHz for rural penetration like Jio, with ARPU uplift from digital wallets.
Over five years, our EBITDA margin has compounded from 32.4% in 2018 amid cord-cutting to 37.5% trailing twelve months—a 100 basis point CAGR—as the industry shifts from capex-heavy 4G to opex-leveraged 5G scale. We anticipate 100-200 basis points annual expansion through 2025 via edge computing with AWS Outposts, ORAN to 50% for 15% vendor cuts, converged telecom-media differentiation versus Netflix's 22% margins, targeting 42% by 2026 through Midwest fiber M&A and buybacks from over 90% free cash flow conversion. Risks include 2024 FCC mid-band auctions and ad softness if CPI exceeds 3%, but we're committed to 37-39% full-year guidance with 5G enterprise upside.
Turning to subscriber acquisition cost trends, our blended SAC across mobile, fixed broadband, and streaming came in at $458 per subscriber, a 15% year-over-year decline and 7% sequential improvement from Q1's $492, at the lower end of guidance and ahead of AT&T's $550 postpaid or Comcast's mid-$400s broadband. Wireless postpaid SAC was $512, down 18% year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter, with 1.2 million net adds on Unlimited Max 5G plans. Optimized device subsidies capped iPhone 15 promotions at 50% off for high-ARPU prospects, reducing average subsidy 22% to $285, paired with performance-based digital marketing on Google DV360 and Meta Advantage+ for 28% cost-per-acquisition efficiency uplift. In the US at 65% of adds, SAC stabilized at $495 amid T-Mobile competition, but Paramount+ bundling controlled spend; Europe was $540 from Vodafone synergies and EU roaming compliance, lowered by 5G SA campaigns cutting acquisition churn 3 percentage points.
Fixed broadband SAC at $372 declined 12% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with 850,000 net adds from fiber overbuilds and Charter co-marketing. Reduced truck-rolls via self-install app at 62% adoption and Palantir geospatial AI dropped US SAC to $355 versus Verizon Fios $380; APAC joint venture with Singtel hit $290 on gigabit uptake, while LATAM rose to $420 on inflation but Claro integration sped paybacks 15% via wireless cross-sell.
Streaming/video SAC at $118 fell 8% year-over-year, flat sequentially, adding 2.1 million TeleStream SVOD subs blending linear and ad-supported tiers like Peacock. Disney bundle drove 40% of adds at $85 incremental SAC using ESPN+ UFC rights; FAST channels acquired 25% at near-zero cost organically. North America at $110 from mobile upsells, EMEA at $145 from Sky Italia competition and Bundesliga localization.
Tailwinds included 35% reallocation of $2.1 billion SAC to owned channels like email and in-app referrals, cutting paid search 19% for 4.2x ROAS; Snowflake-Salesforce CDP enabled personalized offers reducing SAC 11% for families, with 5G mmWave cutting post-acquisition churn 2.5 percentage points for 7.8-month payback versus 9.2 last year and $4.20 monthly ARPU uplift. US trends strongest at 14% drop on FCC rural subsidies, APAC/EMEA 10% via telco-media convergence like BT Sport, LATAM 5% uptick offset by 20% ARPU from inflation pricing. Q3 guidance is $440-$460 blended SAC, supporting 12-15% EBITDA expansion at 1.8% churn versus Netflix 2.5% or Verizon 1.0%.
On net subscriber additions, we delivered 378,000 total across residential and business, up 15% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, from our $12 billion capex on 5G Ultra Wideband, XGS-PON fiber to 55% footprint, and content bundling against cord-cutting. Residential at 312,000 net adds—82% of total, strongest in two years—included broadband +245,000, with Fios fiber +180,000 at 42% Northeast/Mid-Atlantic penetration toward 10 million passings; 22% YoY growth from 2 Gig Disney+/Hulu bundles at 0.85% monthly churn. 5G Home FWA added 65,000 in Southeast rural using 2021 C-band mmWave against T-Mobile and Starlink. Wireless postpaid +112,000 with phones +95,000 at $58.45 ARPU up 3.2% on iPhone 15/S24 Ultra; prepaid +17,000 via SafeLink ACP; linear video -45,000 or 5% YoY down, offset by streaming +20,000 at 25% 'Now TV' super-bundle attachment ($95/month with 2 Gig, unlimited wireless, ad-supported Peacock/Netflix/Apple TV+). Northeast 45% of adds from NYC/Philly fiber over 60% penetration; West Coast 22% countering AT&T/Google Fiber with mmWave; Europe Vodafone JV +12,000 German broadband. Residential churn 1.1% quarterly below 1.4% US average via AI propensity modeling retaining 15% more at-risk.
Business at +66,000 up 5% year-over-year included broadband/ethernet +42,000 with SMB +28,000 on Gigabit Pro at 35% US small business symmetrical multi-gig; enterprise ethernet +14,000 on SD-WAN for AWS Direct Connect/Microsoft Azure. Wireless business +18,000 with private 5G +12,000 like Delta Airlines airports and GM Industry 4.0 on CBRS; 5G Edge MEC with Nokia converting 40% pilots, ARPU $142 up 12%. Midwest 28% from industrial IoT reshoring, South 25% Texas energy private LTE, APAC Singapore +6,000 financial backhaul. Business churn 1.3% from Lumen/Crown Castle poaching, stabilized by 99.999% fiber SLA at 92% net retention.
Converged IP bundling lifted cross-sell to 68% adding $4.50 ARPU; ORAN 5G core at 70% markets enables slicing. Q4 residential guide 350,000-400,000 with 15 million fiber passings and 500,000 FWA; business 70,000-80,000 on 5G SA and edge M&A like BlueJeans. Gaining share versus T-Mobile 28% postpaid via 260 million 5G POPS 40% faster speeds, cable via fiber, Peacock NFL stemming video losses. $18 billion 2023-2025 capex with 22% fiber ROIC builds 6G ecosystem.
New product launches generated $285 million incremental revenue, 18% of quarterly growth and 112% year-over-year from $134 million, boosting wireless to $4.2 billion up 9.5% quarter-over-quarter and broadband/media to $1.8 billion for $7.1 billion total up 8%. Ultra 5G Home FWA in 15 MSAs using C-band/mmWave for gigabit to cord-cutters/rural with edge for gaming/AR/VR like T-Mobile but proprietary; StreamMax bundle 5G Unlimited with VidStream Netflix/Disney+-like at $75/month zero-rated; Enterprise IoT Edge with Siemens/AWS private 5G AI analytics. Wireless $162 million uplift (Ultra $95 million 65% margins virtualized RAN); media/bundles $98 million (StreamMax $72 million, bundled ARPU $82.50 up 7.2% 25% upsell); enterprise $25 million 45% SaaS margins. Added 2.1 million net subs to 52.4 million postpaid up 4.1%, postpaid mobile +1.3 million (65% StreamMax, 0.72% churn ML personalization); broadband/FWA +650,000 Ultra 28% launch penetration vs Comcast DOCSIS; enterprise IoT +45,000 92% retention. Strongest organic since 2020 5G NSA reversing price wars/Starlink.
North America 85% impact, Northeast/Midwest 70% FWA 15% rural penetration, California +250,000 StreamMax 2-point Charter share; Europe 10% UK/Germany +180,000 Premier League; APAC 5% Japan +120,000 $50 billion IoT 22% CAGR. Blended ARPU $68.20 up 5.8%, bundles cut price sensitivity 22%; 5G SA 75% footprint 45% lower latency cloud gaming Xbox. Gaining 1.5 postpaid share YTD vs AT&T FWA/Verizon premium; $1.2 billion capex 6G/ORAN for 20% new service margins 2025, 1.2 GHz mid-band mitigates refarming risks.
Service revenue grew 4.7% year-over-year to $14.2 billion, underlying 5.1% excluding FX/spectrum auctions like Verizon/AT&T. Wireless +3.2% to $8.9 billion on 456,000 postpaid phones to 112 million base, ARPU $52.34 up 2.1% premium 5G Unlimited Max 28% mix from 22%, 5G Home Fusion bundling cut churn 0.79% low vs peers. US Northeast/Southeast 4.5% C-band 85% utilization like T-Mobile SA; LATAM Claro Brasil +6.8% local currency prepaid-postpaid Netflix/Disney+ zero-rated vs Vivo/TIM. Open RAN Nokia/Ericsson 20% capex cut, AWS edge gaming/AR/VR enterprise.
Broadband +5.8% to $3.1 billion outpacing Comcast/Charter, +312,000 consumer adds fiber 18 million passings 4.2 million gigabit 1.2 Gbps ARPU $78.50 up 4.2% 2-gig/multi-gig 35% Paramount+/Peacock bundles. FWA +178,000 to 1.1 million mmWave/C-band Midwest/Appalachia 22% share vs DSL; Europe UK Vodafone FTTP 2,000 communities +7.2% vs BT. $2.8 billion 2024 capex 5 million fiber, 10% CAGR to 2026, BEAD $1 billion rural.
Enterprise +7.1% to $2.2 billion SDN/5G private, $450 million Fortune 50 SD-WAN retailer, Google Cloud 5G MEC sub-5ms; strategic unit +12% automotive Siemens/media NBA 4K/8K; wireline 100G ethernet +4.5% AI data centers. North America 75%, APAC +11% subsea Singapore; 0.9% churn MCaaS sticky. 4-6% multi-year algorithm 5G/fiber/FWA/enterprise, ARPU discipline $1.2 billion opex, 16-18% capex spectrum/AI; full-year 4.5-5.5%.
We hold 285 MHz average spectrum top 100 US markets at $0.42/MHz-POP low from FCC 107/trades. Low-band 600/800/850 MHz 72% utilization up from 65% 4G refarm IoT/rural 95% coverage 15% FWA share vs T-Mobile. Mid-band C-band 3.7-3.98/3.45-3.55 CBRS 55% holdings 81% 5G SA massive MIMO Nokia/Samsung spectral efficiency +25% DSS 1.2 Gbps urban, C-band +18pp post $2.1 billion win 12 million 5G subs 22% ARPU premium. mmWave 26/28/39 GHz 42% enterprise/media NFL/Coachella AWS edge +10% small cells. Overall 74% utilization up 9pp vs 68% industry Ookla, 5G traffic 62% up from 45% $4.8 billion wireless +14%.
Northeast/West 85% mid-band premium Peacock bundles like Charter Spectrum Mobile; South/Plains 68% low-band FWA vs Dish to 2 million YE25 $50/month. $1.8 billion FY25 capex 40% spectrum: refarm 40 MHz PCS 1900 to n77 Q4 +30% capacity 50 markets Ericsson AI; Auction 110 3.5 GHz/6 GHz $800 million mid-band FWA 40% 100 million homes vs Cox; Open RAN Qualcomm X100 DSA CBRS 90%+ 2025; mmWave slicing NBC Olympics sub-10ms $200 million B2B; 15% low-band IoT/private Rust Belt, mid-band XR/gaming; Europe Vantage Towers 3.6 GHz JVs. 3.2x NPV five-year, 48% 5G EBITDA 2026.
We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $1.8 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. I would like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage and faster speeds across 260 million POPS with median speeds 40% above peers. Our network reliability remains high at 99.999% SLA, and we are investing in advanced technologies like Open RAN scaling to 50%, AI traffic management improving PUE to 1.35, edge computing alliances with AWS for low-latency gaming and AR, and ORAN-compliant core for virtualized slicing supporting FWA, private networks, and media streaming. We're also focused on optimizing for emerging applications like IoT, Industry 4.0 automation, and 4K/8K remote broadcast, with dynamic spectrum sharing boosting efficiency 25% and 5G SA covering 75-85% footprints.

David Ruiz: Thank you, Lisa. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We saw strong growth in subscriber additions totaling 378,000 net across segments, driven by innovative offerings like Ultra 5G Home, StreamMax bundles, and Enterprise IoT Edge, alongside targeted marketing with 28% CPA uplift and personalized CDP offers. Postpaid adds hit 1.2-1.3 million with 0.72-0.85% churn best in class, broadband/FWA 650,000-850,000, enterprise 45,000-66,000. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, with AI chatbots handling 65% Tier 1 queries and propensity modeling retaining 15% more at-risk, improving experience across touchpoints. We are also expanding partnerships like Disney, Roku FAST, Charter co-marketing, and AWS/Siemens for bundled services enhancing value, lifting cross-sell to 68% and ARPU $4.50+ per household.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your subscriber acquisition costs and your strategy for reducing churn, specifically with regards to your new StreamMax bundles?

David Ruiz: Thanks, Emily. Our blended SAC at $458 reflects 15% year-over-year improvement through optimized subsidies, digital marketing efficiency, and bundle stickiness—StreamMax drove 65% of postpaid mobile adds at lower incremental cost via zero-rated data and content personalization, contributing to 0.72% churn our best in five years. Strategies like family propensity models and 5G mmWave post-acquisition retention cut payback to 7.8 months, with bundles reducing elasticity 22%. We're guiding further declines supporting low churn at 1.8% enterprise-wide.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for leveraging AI and automation to improve network efficiency and reduce operational costs, and how does that impact EBITDA margins?

Lisa Patel: Great question, Raj. AI-driven traffic on Open RAN trials—20% of sites—cut energy 18% or $120 million annualized despite 25% traffic growth, improving PUE to 1.35; GenAI chatbots handled 65% support slashing call costs 22% or $85 million, stabilizing churn at 0.85%. These Efficiency 2.0 levers delivered +300 basis points to our 38.2% margin, with RPA, propensity modeling, and dynamic spectrum sharing scaling to +100-200 basis points annually through 2025 alongside ORAN vendor cuts and edge monetization.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Chris Lopez: Can you discuss the regulatory environment and any potential impacts on your business, including spectrum renewal auctions?

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Chris. The regulatory landscape remains navigable—EU roaming caps and UK Ofcom compressed Europe ARPU 2% but FTTH acquisitions offset; FCC rural subsidies aid US FWA, BEAD could add $1 billion. For 2024 mid-band renewals like Auction 110, our $800 million budget and 285 MHz portfolio at low $0.42/MHz-POP position us strongly, with refarming PCS to n77 and CBRS DSA mitigating risks while enabling 40% FWA coverage. Overall, no material impacts expected, focused on 3.2x NPV from efficient allocation.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities around converged 5G-media, fiber/FWA expansion, and efficiency. We are confident in our ability to deliver sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders, with full-year guidance intact and upside from enterprise ramps. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Subscriber impact: +2.1M net to 52.4M postpaid (+4.1%); postpaid mobile +1.3M, broadband/FWA +650,000, enterprise IoT +45,000. Boosted ARPU $68.20 (+5.8%), reversed price wars.
